citeAs: Gokaslan, Aaron, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, and Volodymyr Kuleshov (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv.
creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (Cornell Tech; Databricks Mosaic)
description: CommonCatalog is an open dataset of roughly 70 million Creative-Commons-licensed images paired with synthetic captions. The images are sourced from YFCC100M/Flickr and curated into commercial and non-commercial splits to train CommonCanvas text-to-image models.
name: CommonCatalog
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors compared several captioning models qualitatively and chose BLIP-2 for caption synthesis. They note BLIP-2 captions were often more descriptive than LAION-2B alt-text and cite corroborating evidence that BLIP-2 captions are higher quality than ground-truth captions, though with reduced diversity.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated for the Creative-Commons images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT model after the authors compared several captioning models and selected BLIP-2 based on qualitative analysis and state-of-the-art MS COCO performance.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that YFCC100M data is about a decade old, so the Creative-Commons images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. It also notes that synthetic BLIP-2 captions have reduced diversity of n-grams and that web-sourced caption styles may not align with human-generated language nuances.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by starting from YFCC100M metadata, using Flickr IDs to re-scrape the original Creative-Commons images from Flickr, excluding non-derivative licenses, and partitioning the remaining data into commercial and non-commercial subsets. The authors then generated synthetic captions for all included images with BLIP-2.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper highlights data incompleteness: most Creative-Commons images lacked the captions needed for text-to-image training, and only about 31% of images had alt text. The missing caption data was addressed by generating synthetic captions with BLIP-2.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia metadata from YFCC100M, with Flickr IDs linking to the original Flickr-hosted content. The authors re-scraped high-resolution images from Flickr based on those IDs.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that Creative-Commons images are relatively scarce compared with LAION, many categories such as faces, general photography, and paintings underperform, synthetic captions have reduced diversity, and the YFCC100M source data is about a decade old and not as current as LAION-2B.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For caption generation, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512x512 pixels before being passed to BLIP-2. The dataset was also filtered by license, excluding non-derivative images and creating commercial and non-commercial splits.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors re-scraped images from Flickr using YFCC100M IDs, filtered out non-derivative licenses, partitioned the data into commercial and non-commercial subsets, and center-cropped and resized images to at most 512x512 for BLIP-2 captioning. At diffusion-model training time, images remained at native resolution.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they plan in the future to augment CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as a way to train text-to-image models using open-licensed images with known provenance, aiming to reduce copyright concerns and improve reproducibility relative to web-scraped datasets such as LAION. The paper also discusses that the model is less likely than SD2 to generate iconic copyrighted characters from suggestive prompts.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and evaluating open text-to-image generative models, specifically the CommonCanvas family of latent diffusion models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT-2.7B / BLIP-2 OPT2.5B pre-trained image captioning model was used to generate synthetic captions for the images.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images of people and public figures; the paper shows the model can generate celebrities such as Bill Gates, Elon Musk, Kim Kardashian, Barack Obama, Hillary Clinton, and Richard Feynman, implying the underlying image data contains human faces and identifiable persons.
